raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview The Step3 tool parser silently drops any parameter whose value contains `<`. This PR makes the parameter regex match up to the closing tag instead of the first `<`. ## Claims - Step3 tool calls keep parameter values that contain `<`, such as `a < 5` or `hi`, in streaming and non-streaming mode. - Values without `<` parse exactly as before. ## Validation New unit test `test_parameter_value_with_angle_bracket`, run in both streaming and non-streaming mode: ```bash python -m pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/test_step3_tool_parser.py ``` | | Result | |---|---| | Before (test only) | `2 failed, 9 passed, 8 xfailed`: `assert {} == {'sql': 'SELECT * FROM t WHERE a < 5', 'html': 'hi'}` | | After | `11 passed, 8 xfailed` | The 8 xfails already exist on main and are unchanged. End-to-end check with a Step3 model (`tool_choice="auto"`, a tool with a string parameter, prompt asking for a SQL query with `<`): Parser check with the real Step3 tokenizer (`stepfun-ai/step3`). A tool call whose `sql` value contains `<` goes through `run_tool_extraction`, the helper the tool parser tests use, in both modes: | Mode | `main` (`arguments`) | This PR (`arguments`) | |---|---|---| | non-streaming | `{}` | `{"sql": "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total < 100"}` | | streaming | `{}` | `{"sql": "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total < 100"}` | On `main` the call is still emitted, but its arguments come back empty, so a client runs the tool with no input. Not run end to end: Step3 has 321B parameters and I have no hardware that can serve it. The change is confined to the parameter regex, which the check above drives with the model's real tokenizer.
Reproduction script import json from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager from tests.tool_parsers.utils import run_tool_extraction tok = get_tokenizer("stepfun-ai/step3") out = ("<｜tool_calls_begin｜><｜tool_call_begin｜>function<｜tool_sep｜>" '' 'SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total < 100' "<｜tool_call_end｜><｜tool_calls_end｜>") for streaming in (False, True): parser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("step3")(tok) _, calls = run_tool_extraction(parser, out, streaming=streaming) print(streaming, [json.loads(c.function.arguments or "{}") for c in calls])
## Details Root cause: `_parse_steptml_invoke` matched values with `([^<]*)`, so the regex failed on any value containing `<` and the parameter was skipped without a log line. The value group is now `(.*?)` with `re.DOTALL`. It ends at the first ``, and multi-line values still match as before. Limit: a value that contains the literal text `` still ends early. The format has no escaping, so this cannot be fixed in the parser. Not a duplicate: I searched open and closed PRs for "step3 tool parser" and issues and PRs for "steptml". #49567 (whitespace in Step3 values) only removes `.strip()` and keeps `[^<]*`. #55115 and #57809 change streaming bookkeeping, not the regex. #55175 changes test fixtures only. No issue reports this bug. Co-author: Claude ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

- #60968: Step3 tool calls drop any argument value that contains "<"
- #60969: truncated K2 Horizon output comes back as content in non-streaming mode but as reasoning when streaming

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

LGTM from my side. Tested at `b15510d`.

I also regrouped the streaming deltas (1, 2, 3, 8 tokens, whole output at once). The new test fails only when the whole output is one delta, and existing tests fail the same way on main, so that part is #55082. On top of #55115, the Step3 tests give 13 passed, 8 xfailed at every split.

The conflicts with #49567, #55115 and #57809 are only the test additions at the end of `test_step3_tool_parser.py`.
